note:
Paper 75, Team 32879, a 2015 search-theory paper about finding a missing aircraft over open ocean. Thirty-two measured regions over twenty-four of the thirty-five pages: thirty figure rows and two refusals, nothing left unaccounted for and nothing unresolved. The paper prints no tables at all, so this is the lane's first census entry in a while with an empty table list beside a full figure list.

What the exhibits are. Thirteen line plots carry the model comparisons: the prior and posterior overlay of Figure 6, the cumulative-and-daily pair printed five times over (Figures 10, 12, 16, 20 and 25), and the seven multi-model comparisons from Figure 21 to Figure 28. Six 3-D mesh surfaces carry the probability densities before and after searching. Seven drawings carry the geometry the paper argues with: the glide-angle and bearing sketches of Figure 1, the glide-slope triangle, the corridor figures, the spiral and the octagonal sector. One contour map, Figure 7, carries the mass distribution itself, and three composites - Figures 8, 14 and 18 - pair a contour panel with a drawing of the search that produced it.

The two refusals are both page furniture that the measurer could not tell from artwork: the cover's 'For office use only' registration block, and the letterhead of the closing letter to commercial airlines. Neither carries a number or a caption.

What the paper gets wrong, and what the census therefore has to declare rather than repair. The printed figure numbers run 2 to 24 and then 26 to 28: there is no Figure 25 anywhere, and the only exhibit that can be it is the unnumbered (a)/(b) pair on p27. Figure 1 is in the same state - two separately captioned panels, cited in prose as 'Figures 1a & 1b' and never printed with a number of its own. Figure 28's subsection has no heading, so its section path stops one level short. And the paper's own plot titles disagree with its captions in small ways that a reader would trip over: Figure 16's title prints 'Square Spriral Search Model', Figure 21's caption says Direct Model Comparison while the plot is titled Single Plane Model Comparison, and the p27 pair is titled Small Plane Model Comparison although the aircraft under discussion is a V-22 Osprey.

Two reading difficulties are worth recording because they cost time. Fourteen raster figures are MATLAB exports whose axis text is part of the bitmap, so it reads only from a crop; the thirteen vector plots by contrast have their axis and legend text in the layer, with the y-axis label always printed mirrored - 'ytilibaborP' rather than 'Probability' - which is why the geometry dump for those pages looks like noise. And the text layer interleaves the two p27 captions line by line, so neither can be quoted as a contiguous string; both are typed from the crop instead.

Citation practice is thin: six figures are named by number in the whole paper, and the rest are introduced by a deictic sentence immediately above the art. That is not a defect in the paper so much as a property of its genre, but it does mean the mention column here is mostly empty and should not be read as a measurement of how often the figures are used.
rules: Families are read off the page, not off the captions, and the captions repeat: thirteen rows are line plots, seven are schematic drawings, six are 3-D surfaces, one is a contour plot and three are composites. Fourteen captions print the same two sentences - 'Probability Density Distribution after a 5-day search' four times and 'Cumulative Probability of Success after a 20-day search' five times - so a caption alone never fixes a family here [geometry.family].

The 3-D surfaces are all one kind: six mesh surfaces exported from MATLAB, each drawn over an x/y frame in miles with a plain Probability axis and none carrying a colour bar, so 'surface-mesh' is the whole class rather than a per-figure judgement [geometry.three_d].

Three rows hold two panels of different families - a filled contour beside a geometric search-path drawing - and all three are laid out as a row of two: Figures 8, 14 and 18. The rest of the multi-panel work is single-family and keeps its family with a panel count of one, because each panel is its own caption or its own figure [geometry.panel_layout].

Every figure caption prints BELOW its artwork, in all thirty captioned rows, and no exhibit in this paper is a table - the only ruled grid is the cover's registration block, which is refused. So the caption side is uniform where the families are not [caption.position].

Numbering is not uniform. Twenty-six rows carry the printed form 'Figure N:' with the colon, but four rows carry subcaptions only: the pair on p5 prints '(a) Visual definition of theta.' and '(b) Visual definition of phi.', and the pair on p27 prints '(a)' and '(b) Comparison of Search Patterns for Single Small Plane...'. Neither pair prints its own figure number anywhere on the page, so both are recorded with numbering 'none' [caption.numbering].

The printed numbers skip one. Captions run Figure 2 to Figure 24 and then Figure 26 to Figure 28, with no 'Figure 25' printed anywhere in the paper, and the p27 pair under 3.7.4 is the only exhibit the missing number can belong to - two panels of the same comparison at full and zoomed scale, which is what that section's prose introduces. The census counts them as two rows and says so here rather than inventing a caption [caption.numbering].

Only six printed figures are ever named by number in prose: Figure 2 on p5, Figure 3 on p7, Figure 6 on p11, Figure 14 on p19 and Figure 22 on p25, plus one lower-case 'from figure 8' on p15 which is recorded as it prints. Everything else is pointed at deictically - 'shown below', 'the following figure', 'Consider now the following figure' - so twenty-four rows carry an empty mention block [mention.count].

Two exhibits lead their section by a page: Figure 2's caption prints on p6 while its citation prints on p5, and Figure 3's caption prints on p8 while its citation prints on p7 - the prose introducing the contour plot on p7 is the only place Figure 3 is named [mention.lead_pages].

Section paths come from the printed headings and not from the ctx index, which was fooled four times on this paper: '0.8 Rectangular Model' and '0.9 Rectangular Model' are legend lines from the comparison plots, '0.18 Octagonal Sector Model Octagonal Sector Model' is the axis tick and legend of Figure 25, and '747 Crash' is a legend entry on p31. All four are replaced by the real chain here [place.section_path].

Figure 28's section has no heading at all. The 3.7.x run ends with 3.7.6 The Effectiveness Parameter on p29 and 4 Final Remarks opens on p32, and p31 carries only the plot and its caption, so the row stops at '3.7 Model Variation and Comparison' instead of borrowing the preceding subsection's name [place.section_path].

Captions were copied out of the layer with their curly quotation marks intact - Figures 13, 14, 17 and 18 all quote a search pattern in quotes - and the two p5 subcaptions carry real Greek letters, theta and phi, not the private-use glyphs that spoil the Greek in the body prose of this paper [caption.verbatim].

Area does nothing to separate exhibits here. The six surfaces are the biggest boxes on their pages - the p8 one at 0.245 of the page and the p16 and p20 ones at 0.243 and 0.249 - while the two refusals are 0.069 and 0.136, so the cover block and the letterhead sit inside the same size band as real exhibits and only the crop could tell them apart [place.area_frac].
